advisories.auditPatchedVersionDisplay: <0.0.0; this display is not proof that no patched release exists.
advisories.conditions: A victim activates a link inside the native WebView leading to its own-origin internal HTTP proxy path; attacker-selected remote document is returned under application origin and may access origin storage/native plugins. Disabling CapacitorHttp alone is explicitly insufficient.
sourceEvidence: apps/mobile/package.json:26-42 declares runtime Android/iOS/core and native plugins
apps/mobile/index.html:28 embeds web-app-frame without a sandbox attribute
apps/mobile/src/main.ts sets frame.src from configured webAppOrigin and guards deep-link origin at lines123-135
No shouldOverrideLoad or internal-proxy-path mitigation found in apps/mobile Java/Swift/Kotlin/TypeScript/JSON source
advisories.exposureConclusion: Native runtime dependency is real, not merely a test dependency. No exploit through this application's actual UI was performed; released native binary versions and effective configuration are unknown. No Capacitor imports found in web/API production source.
advisories.installedEvidence: CI frozen lock and generated native integration references establish resolved versions. Native node_modules links are absent in the reviewed QA worktree; no local native runtime was executed.
advisories.priority: Resolve before distributing a native app built from this vulnerable runtime; do not present this as an established e-code.ai HTTP exploit.
advisories.candidateRemediation: Move coordinated Capacitor core/CLI/platform packages to a maintained patched 8.x release, regenerate native projects via official sync, test native navigation and registered plugins, rebuild and redistribute. No dependency change made.

advisories.conditions: Requires a prior Object.prototype pollution primitive; inherited execArgv or env can become explicit worker options and load attacker-controlled code.
sourceEvidence: Tinypool1.1.1 dist/index.js:509 builds a normal-prototype options object; lines547-549 read env/execArgv

Installed Vitest3.2.6 forks/threads constructors explicitly provide own env and execArgv (coverage.DfSpMS-b.js:2616-2622,2751-2758), so the advisory alone does not prove this exact injection chain in standard Vitest use
advisories.exposureConclusion: Tooling/CI supply-chain risk. A prerequisite pollution source and reachable attacker-controlled worker code have not been established in this repository. No Tinypool web/API request handler found.

advisories.conditions: Requires prior Object.prototype.filename pollution and pool.run(task, options) with a supplied options object lacking an own filename. run(task) without a second argument is not affected by this vector according to the advisory.
sourceEvidence: Tinypool1.1.1 dist/index.js:748-750 destructures filename from run options without own-property checks
Installed Vitest3.2.6 calls pool.run(data,{name,channel}) for forks and pool.run(data,{transferList,name,channel}) for threads (coverage.DfSpMS-b.js:2652,2793): options have no own filename
advisories.exposureConclusion: A documented gadget is present in actual test tooling. No prerequisite prototype-pollution entry point was proved, and no remote web/API exploit was established. Priority is tooling hardening, not a claim of platform compromise.

tinypoolDependencyPaths.classification: All 15 direct Vitest3.2.6 declarations are devDependencies; services/api invokes the root tooling without declaring Vitest itself.
tinypoolDependencyPaths.mobileTestTooling: apps/mobile uses Vitest4.1.5; that lockfile snapshot has no Tinypool dependency.
tinypoolDependencyPaths.candidateRemediation: Update the test tooling coherently to a compatible dependency tree without the vulnerable Tinypool versions, or validate an upstream backport. Tinypool >=2.1.2 covers both advisories, but a blind major override of Vitest3.2.6's ^1.1.1 dependency is not a validated fix.
